methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs an exceptionally comprehensive multi-platform approach integrating primary patient-derived tissues (114 ccRCC + paired normal kidney samples from the Erlangen RCC cohort), TCGA KIRC/KIRP/KICH public cohort analyses, primary tubule and tumor cell isolation from 34 individual patients, ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq/CUT&Tag, HIF ChIP-seq/CUT&Tag, RNA-seq, CRISPR/Cas9 enhancer knockout in both cell lines (786-0, RCC4) and primary ccRCC cells, reporter gene assays, xenograft tumor models, eQTL analysis linking rs12617313 genotype to HIF-2α expression in KIRC (n=403 patients) and primary tubule cells (n=105 donors), ABC enhancer-promoter modeling, and Cicero co-accessibility analysis. Multiple complementary approaches converge on the same conclusion. Statistical methods include two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction, Spearman correlation, chi-squared tests, and DESeq2 with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. Limitations include absence of formal power calculations, RNA-seq experiments in knock-out clones performed with only n=2 clones per condition, and xenograft experiments using NOD/SCID gamma immunodeficient mice.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This mechanistic study has direct clinical implications for ccRCC, a disease for which HIF-2 inhibitors (belzutifan) are now FDA/EMA-approved. The identification of a ccRCC-specific EPAS1 enhancer that governs tumor growth in xenografts establishes a potential therapeutic target for belzutifan-resistant tumors (which can arise through EPAS1 or HIF-1β mutations). The eQTL analysis linking rs12617313 genotype to HIF-2α expression in 403 KIRC patients provides population-level evidence that this regulatory circuit is operative in human tumors. EPAS1-enhancer 2 accessibility correlating with HIF-2α mRNA levels could serve as a biomarker for HIF-2 inhibitor sensitivity. Evidence level is 4 (retrospective patient cohort analyses with mechanistic cell/animal model validation) with no prospective clinical trial data.

reporting_quality.justification: A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Animal experiments are conducted under a named ethics license (55.2.2-2532-2-2150-19) with sex-matched littermates and described randomization and blinding. All antibody catalog numbers, software versions, and bioinformatic pipeline parameters are provided. RNA integrity numbers and sequencing depth statistics are provided in supplementary data. Primary tissue use is covered by two named ethics approvals (329_16B, 542_20Bc) with patient written informed consent. Source data files are explicitly provided. Published datasets are integrated with GEO accession numbers. Minor limitations: formal power calculations absent, n=2 clones for some RNA-seq experiments is acknowledged, and the genotyping array cannot resolve all fine-mapped GWAS variants.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first systematic characterization of transcriptional enhancers driving EPAS1/HIF-2α overexpression in ccRCC, filling a notable gap since protein-level regulation via VHL has been extensively studied but mRNA dysregulation remained unexplored. The discovery of a ccRCC-specific auto-regulatory feed-forward transcriptional circuit — where HIF-2 promotes its own expression via EPAS1-enhancer E2 in concert with renal lineage factors PAX8 and HNF-1β — is mechanistically novel. The genetic interaction with the RCC risk SNP rs12617313 as an eQTL operating in a HIF-dependent manner provides a molecular explanation for a decade-old GWAS finding. The demonstration that EPAS1-enhancer 2 is indispensable for xenograft tumor growth and overlaps with belzutifan response genes has direct translational relevance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically organized, progressing from clinical observation (HIF-2α mRNA overexpression in ccRCC) through epigenomic discovery (ccRCC-activated EPAS1 enhancer) to mechanistic dissection (HIF, PAX8, HNF-1β binding) to genetic interaction (eQTL) to in vivo relevance (xenograft, downstream transcriptional output). The model figure (Fig. 7i) clearly summarizes the transcriptional circuit. Statistical reporting is rigorous with effect sizes, confidence intervals, and exact p-values throughout. The discussion cogently contextualizes therapeutic implications for belzutifan resistance. Minor weaknesses: some methods sections are very dense and some figure legends are long, but these are appropriate for a high-complexity multi-platform study.

key_strengths: First comprehensive mechanistic characterization of transcriptional regulatory enhancers driving EPAS1/HIF-2α mRNA overexpression in ccRCC, explaining how VHL loss triggers HIF-2α transcriptional autoregulation via a feed-forward circuit with PAX8 and HNF-1β

Exceptional breadth of orthogonal evidence: ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP/CUT&Tag, HIF ChIP/CUT&Tag, CRISPR enhancer knockout in primary patient cells and cell lines, reporter assays, xenograft models, eQTL analysis in 403 KIRC patients, and Cicero co-accessibility — all converging on the same conclusion

Direct translation of GWAS finding: rs12617313 (the EPAS1 RCC risk SNP most tightly linked to VHL mutations) functions as a HIF-dependent eQTL for EPAS1 expression in both KIRC tumors and primary tubule cells, providing the first molecular explanation for its cancer predisposition mechanism

Clinical relevance for belzutifan-resistant ccRCC: EPAS1-enhancer 2 activity correlates with HIF-2α expression, transcriptional output overlaps with PT2385 effects, and enhancer targeting prevented xenograft growth, establishing the locus as a potential therapeutic target for resistance bypass
Rigorous use of primary patient-derived cells (34 individual ccRCC/tubule pairs, 105 primary tubule cell isolates) rather than relying solely on established cell lines
key_concerns: Xenograft experiments use NOD/SCID-gamma immunodeficient mice; the impact of the EPAS1 enhancer on tumor growth in an immunocompetent context is not assessed

RNA-seq experiments comparing enhancer-knockout effects in single cell clones use only n=2 clones per condition, limiting the ability to distinguish clone-specific from enhancer-specific transcriptional effects

The precise mechanism through which rs12617313 risk allele A modulates HIF-dependent EPAS1 activation (direct motif disruption, local chromatin state alteration, long-range interaction) is not resolved
Extension to glioblastoma is supported only by correlative ATAC-seq and eQTL data with limited mechanistic follow-up; the therapeutic implication for GBM remains speculative
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is an exceptionally high-quality mechanistic study that elegantly combines multi-omics approaches with patient-derived primary cells to define a novel transcriptional autoregulatory circuit governing EPAS1/HIF-2α expression in ccRCC, with direct implications for understanding genetic cancer predisposition and overcoming HIF-2 inhibitor resistance. The convergent evidence across patient cohorts, primary cells, established cell lines, and in vivo models supports Tier 1 consideration with minor revisions to address clone number limitations in RNA-seq experiments.
